the effect of MC on mechanical parameters is greater for latewood than for earlywood and that the tensile properties of the earlywood and late wood can be determined independently from those of the samples containing both early- and latewood.

the effect of MC on mechanical parameters is different in earlywood and late wood and that the mechanical parameters of wood containing both earlywood zones and latewood zones are close to the values calculated from the rule-of-mixtures.
the tensile properties of earlywood of Scots pine are similar in dry and wet state, but the mechanical properties of latewood of Scots Pine are significantly affected by the MC.

the effect of MC on mechanical properties of early and latewood of pine and the effect of the rule of mixtues on the calculation of these properties.
the mechanical properties of Scots pine wood subjected to tension in the direction of the fibers, and the effect of the wood moisture content on its mechanical properties.
the effect of MC on tensile properties of earlywood, latewood, and the mixture of both zones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the studied Scots pine wood samples of both low and high MC, the tensile properties of earlywood were similar to the properties of latewood.
, for the studied properties, MC has greater influence on latewood than on earlywood and the effect on the mechanical properties is greater in samples containing both early- and latewood.
the effect of MC on tensile properties of Scots pine is not significant, and that the rule of mixures may be used for calculating the properties of earlywood, latewood and wood containing both zones.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tensile properties of earlywood or late wood of Scots pine wood in wet and dry states can be determined individually, or as a weighted mean for the whole wood.
the rule of mixtues may be applied to calculate the mechanical parameters of earlywood and of latewood of Scots Pine.
the tensile properties of wood are not significantly different for earlywood and for latewood and that the tensile strength of wood is not influenced by its moisture content.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanical properties of the earlywood and latewoods of Scots pine can be considered as a single material when the mechanical properties of wood samples with both zones are determined.
it is necessary to determine the mechanical properties of individual wood zones in order to correctly evaluate the properties of wood containing both earlywood zones and latewood zones.
the rule of mixures may be used for the prediction of tensile properties along the grains of Scots pine wood in dry and wet states.
